evidence.claim: Wolfspeed reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of about $150 million, GAAP gross margin of negative 27%, GAAP net loss of $120 million, operating cash flow of negative $84 million, and $1.2 billion of cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments as of March 29, 2026.
evidence.source_title: Wolfspeed Reports Financial Results for the Third Quarter of Fiscal 2026

evidence.claim: Wolfspeed said AI data-center applications grew approximately 30% sequentially in Q3 FY2026 and described the area as a moderate but expanding part of the business with long-term potential.
evidence.source_title: Wolfspeed Reports Financial Results for the Third Quarter of Fiscal 2026

evidence.claim: Wolfspeed launched what it described as the first commercially available 10 kV SiC power MOSFET for grid modernization, industrial electrification, and AI data-center infrastructure.
evidence.source_title: Wolfspeed Reports Financial Results for the Third Quarter of Fiscal 2026

evidence.claim: Wolfspeed introduced its TOLT top-side-cooled package portfolio, positioned for higher power density and thermal performance in next-generation AI data centers and rack power applications.
evidence.source_title: Wolfspeed Unveils Next-Gen TOLT Portfolio to Address Surging AI Datacenter Demand

evidence.claim: Wolfspeed announced a dedicated data-center solutions team and Silicon Valley regional office, with hires focused on hyperscalers, ODM ecosystems, and high-density AI cluster power solutions.
evidence.source_title: Wolfspeed Launches Dedicated Data Center Solutions Team in Silicon Valley; Hires Industry Experts to Drive Highly Compact and Efficient Power Solutions for AI Infrastructure

evidence.claim: Wolfspeed announced that its 300mm SiC technology platform could serve as a materials enabler for advanced AI and HPC heterogeneous packaging by the end of the decade and said it was engaging ecosystem partners to evaluate the technology.
evidence.source_title: Wolfspeed Unveils Foundation for Next-Generation AI Data Center Advanced Packaging Leveraging 300mm Silicon Carbide Technology

evidence.claim: Wolfspeed completed its financial restructuring and emerged from Chapter 11 protection on September 29, 2025, stating that total debt was reduced by about 70% and maturities were extended to 2030.
evidence.source_title: Wolfspeed Successfully Completes Financial Restructuring, Emerges as Financially Stronger Company Well Positioned in Silicon Carbide Market

evidence.claim: Wolfspeed announced March 2026 private placements of $379 million of convertible notes and about $96.9 million of common stock and pre-funded warrants, with proceeds intended to redeem higher-cost senior notes and support diversification into AI data centers, industrial and energy, and aerospace and defense markets.
evidence.source_title: Wolfspeed Announces Subscriptions for $379 Million of Convertible Notes and $96.9 Million of Common Stock and Pre-Funded Warrants

evidence.claim: Wolfspeed's Q3 FY2026 SEC-filed earnings exhibit lists risks including recent Chapter 11 emergence, customer/vendor retention, production yields, underutilization, design-in conversion, EV adoption risk, and the ability to diversify into medium- to high-voltage verticals such as AI data centers.
evidence.source_title: Wolfspeed Q3 FY2026 Earnings Release Exhibit 99.1

memory_update.text: WOLF maps to New Hotspots primarily through SiC power devices for AI data-center rack power, high-voltage grid/industrial electrification, and potential 300mm SiC advanced-packaging materials; keep in speculative_shadow lane until revenue scale and customer qualification improve.

WOLF is not a direct transformer/switchgear bottleneck; it is a second-order power-semiconductor supplier that could benefit if data-center and grid architectures require more efficient high-voltage conversion.
Need AI/data-center revenue dollars, not just percentage growth. A 30% sequential increase is insufficient without base size, customer concentration, and margin contribution.
Need verification of commercial traction for 10 kV SiC MOSFETs and TOLT packages through named OEM, ODM, UPS, inverter, hyperscaler, or utility-equipment design wins.

Need runway and dilution model after March 2026 refinancing: cash burn, debt service, convertibles, warrants, operating cash flow, underutilization costs, and margin recovery should be tracked before upgrading WOLF from speculative_shadow.
300mm SiC advanced-packaging exposure is long-dated optionality. Require partner names, reliability data, cost roadmap, and integration proof before treating it as a Serenity chokepoint.

summary: Candidate chunk mapped for Wolfspeed (WOLF). Relationship to New Hotspots is real but still speculative-shadow rather than core bottleneck: Wolfspeed has direct SiC product exposure to AI data-center rack power, grid modernization, industrial electrification, and potential advanced AI/HPC packaging materials, but the investable signal is weakened by recent Chapter 11 emergence, negative gross margin, operating cash burn, and unproven scale of AI/data-center revenue. The main Serenity question is whether WOLF is becoming a high-voltage/data-center power-conversion beneficiary, or whether the story is mostly a pivot narrative masking underutilization and automotive-cycle pressure.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Quantify AI/data-center revenue dollars, design wins, customer names or customer types, ODM/hyperscaler pull-through, gross margin by product family, and whether sequential AI data-center growth is from a small base.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check FY2026 Q4 call, FY2026 10-K, customer-design-win disclosures, distributor sell-through, and any hyperscaler/ODM qualification references for TOLT, U2, or other top-side cooled SiC packages.
ticker_relationships.node: data-center power conversion and rack-level power density
ticker_relationships.relationship: Wolfspeed sells SiC power devices and launched a TOLT package portfolio positioned for AI/hyperscale data-center power supplies; this gives WOLF direct exposure to higher-density rack power architectures, but the current revenue contribution appears early-stage and not yet proven as a large business mix shift.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether 10 kV SiC devices are shipping in commercial volumes, whether utilities/inverter OEMs are designing them into grid or data-center equipment, and whether pricing/margins exceed legacy silicon or IGBT alternatives.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Look for qualification announcements from inverter, UPS, solid-state transformer, medium-voltage drive, or power-conversion OEMs; compare with Infineon, onsemi, STMicroelectronics, Rohm, and Mitsubishi SiC roadmaps.
ticker_relationships.node: grid modernization, high-voltage power semiconductors, and industrial electrification
ticker_relationships.relationship: Wolfspeed introduced a commercially available 10 kV SiC MOSFET for grid modernization, industrial electrification, and AI data-center infrastructure, making it a possible second-order beneficiary of grid and data-center power buildouts rather than a direct transformer/switchgear bottleneck.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Foundry/OSAT/system-architect partner identities, reliability data, cost versus silicon/glass/organic substrates, integration pathway, and whether adoption is plausible before the end of the decade.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track partner evaluation updates, patents, conference papers, advanced-packaging ecosystem references, and any named OSAT/foundry collaboration involving SiC interposers or heat spreaders.
ticker_relationships.node: advanced AI/HPC packaging materials and thermal/electrical substrate innovation
ticker_relationships.relationship: Wolfspeed is exploring 300mm SiC substrates as a potential material platform for future AI/HPC heterogeneous packaging, interposers, and heat-spreading use cases. This is a long-dated optionality node, not yet a validated revenue bottleneck.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Actual 200mm utilization, yields, customer capacity reservations, CHIPS/IRA tax-credit realization, customer preference for U.S.-sourced SiC, and whether domestic supply commands pricing power.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify capacity utilization, yield commentary, Section 48D/CHIPS incentive cash receipts, customer prepayment or reservation agreements, and backlog/design-in conversion in future filings.
ticker_relationships.node: domestic SiC substrate and power-device supply chain resilience
ticker_relationships.relationship: Wolfspeed’s U.S.-based SiC substrate and 200mm manufacturing footprint could be strategically relevant if domestic, non-China, high-performance power semiconductor supply becomes a policy or customer procurement bottleneck.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Runway versus cash burn, debt maturity schedule, dilution from convertibles/warrants, gross-margin recovery, underutilization costs, and whether AI/data-center growth can offset EV/automotive softness before liquidity tightens again.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Update liquidity bridge after FY2026 Q4, reconcile convertible/warrant dilution, monitor gross margin trajectory, and compare operating cash flow against stated self-funded business plan.
ticker_relationships.relationship: The company is itself a distressed-capacity node: it emerged from Chapter 11 in September 2025 and still reported negative gross margin, net losses, and negative operating cash flow in Q3 FY2026. This makes the theme relationship high-risk even if the end-market exposure is improving.
